findings.F1: The book loses on direction, not on fees: over 14,202 daily bars the position's gain before costs averages -0.000240 a day against fees of only 0.000026, so the Sharpe is already -0.31 before costs and -0.34 after.
findings.F2: The short loses most where the forecast is strongest. Short days in the lowest 20-bar momentum quintile (the coin fell most over the prior 20 bars) earn -0.001288 a day (t -1.91, n 1669) at a mean allocation of -0.44. The upper two quintiles earn +0.000058 and -0.000009, so even the short's best states only break even.
findings.F3: The deepest distances below the 200-day average are where the coin rebounds. In the deepest distance quartile, the excess 10-bar return after short blocks is +0.0074 (n 233), and the block gain is -0.0040. The shallower quartiles show excess returns of -0.0071 and -0.0072.
findings.F4: The forecast's grading points the wrong way. The slope of excess 10-bar return on allocation is -0.0126, and the deepest forecast quartile (mean allocation -0.75) has a block gain of -0.0067 (t -0.92). The Spearman correlations of daily gross gain with distance, 20-bar momentum and 5-bar momentum are only 0.010, 0.036 and 0.050.
findings.F5: The book's worst days come from shorting after a crash. The worst 5% of short days (418) sum to -21.56, against a total of -3.77 over all short days. On those days the coin had fallen -14.0% over 20 bars (against -2.0% on all short days) and sat -34.2 below its average (against -15.3).
findings.F6: The losses cluster in rebound years. Short-block gains are t -3.26 in 2020, -2.65 in 2021 and -2.13 in 2023, against +1.59 in 2018, +2.02 in 2019 and +1.42 in 2022. That is why the Sharpe with one window left out stays negative (-0.70).
findings.F7: No state of the short makes the book pay. Short days with a falling 200-day average and positive 20-bar momentum earn +0.000006 a day (n 2410). Short days with a rising average and negative momentum earn -0.001203 (t -2.97, n 1509).

ideas.idea: The further a coin's close sits below its 200-day average, and the more it has fallen over the past weeks, the more it rises over the following days. Its distance below the long average marks exhaustion of the fall, not the continuation of a trend.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to short a coin that is deep below its long average after a sharp fall, and can look to buy it for a rebound that grows with the depth of the fall.
ideas.name: deep-fall rebound below average

ideas.idea: After a coin's close crosses below its 200-day average, the coin keeps falling, more the deeper it sits below the average, only while the coin's recent weeks have been flat to rising rather than a sharp fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should hold the short only after the selling has paused and cut it as the recent fall steepens, which removes the crash-rebound days behind the book's deepest losses.
ideas.name: short only after selling pauses
